text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Four different scenarios are being considered in the opposition camp for their candidate in the presidential elections.
- Cyprus Airways paid the hotel bill for a pilot who grounded his plane in Paphos. He had refused to work an extra 10 minutes in order to fly the plane to Larnaca, its destination.
- A man from Paphos is arrested after tourists were slashed.
- Doubts are raised at the fitness of Greek composer Mikis Theodorakis to perform at a bicommunal concert in Cyprus in June. Theodorakis fell ill with respiratory problems in Germany last week.
- Hellenic Bank is leading a short list of eight bidders with an interest to buy a majority stake in the Bank of Central Greece (Trapeza Kentrikis Ellados).
- The government is expected to give only two licences for casinos once the law is approved by the House of Representatives in the next few months.
- Preparations for direct talks between Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash and President Glafcos Clerides (the Greek Cypriot leader) enter their final stage.
- Citrus farmers in villages of the Nicosia district have uprooted their trees, saying they can no longer compete with cheap imports from Europe.
- The starting point of the United States initiative on Cyprus is the Greco-Turkish differences. U.S. envoy Carey Kavanaugh has important contacts in Ankara and Athens.
- Shopkeepers complain about new opening hours and dividing towns into tourist and non-tourist zones. Shops in tourist zones will be allowed to stay open longer.
- Socialist Edek and centre-left United Democrats have rejected the candidacy of former foreign minister George Iakovou as the opposition's presidential candidate in 1998.
